srs.title: Small Business Payment Platform (India)
srs.summary: Build a role-based payment platform for Indian SMBs offering payment links, transaction reconciliation (T+1), refunds, and reporting. Integrate with a single payment gateway. Evidence supports strict adherence to RBI Digital Payment Security Controls regarding reconciliation timelines (E1, E2), KYC/
assumptions: The 'single gateway' selected will provide native APIs for the required Indian payment channels.
Merchant KYC documents will be provided and valid per RBI Master Direction guidelines (E3).
The single gateway's settlement file format will be compatible with the platform's reconciliation engine designed for E1 standards.
Refund approval workflows will be managed strictly by 'Refund Approver' roles as defined in the brief.
stakeholders: Merchant Admin: Full platform access, manages own business settings.
Refund Approver: Can approve/refund transactions but lacks general admin access.
Support Team: Read-only access for viewing transactions and generating reports for customer support.

requirements.statement: Refund Approver role must have granular permission to approve specific refunds, distinct from viewing transaction details or approving other actions.
requirements.acceptance: Audit logs and permission matrix show 'approve refund' as a distinct, restricted action separate from 'view transaction' or 'initiate refund'.

requirements.statement: Transaction reconciliation must process all digital payment transactions within 24 hours of settlement file receipt.
requirements.acceptance: 95% of reconciliation reports generated within 24 hours; zero successful transactions remain un-reconciled beyond 24 hours for a consecutive 30-day period.

requirements.statement: Integration must connect to a single primary payment gateway only.
requirements.acceptance: System successfully processes test transactions via the designated single gateway; no configuration options or active connections exist for secondary or multiple aggregators.

requirements.acceptance: System automatically rejects walk-in customer registration and transaction initiation for amounts >= 50,000 INR; 0% compliance breaches observed in 1,000 simulated walk-in attempts

requirements.acceptance: System admin panel includes a scheduled review task that generates a report due every 12 months; missed reviews trigger high-priority alerts to senior management.

sdlc.justification: The chosen SDLC is an Agile–V-Model hybrid with a score of 92/100. This model is the optimal fit because the project exhibits a specific combination of high regulatory criticality, high security risk, and a high need for formal verification, which mandates the rigorous phase-gating and documentation formality of the V-Model. Simultaneously, the project suffers from low requirement stability and high expected change frequency, which would render a strict V-Model unviable due to rework costs; Agile addresses this flexibility.
